heroHeadline: Day 29: Bamako Siege Enters Post-Truce Phase; Eid al-Adha Livestock Prices Double; JNIM March 2026 Fuel Deal Expires
heroSubtitle: Day 29 of JNIM's declared 'total siege' of Bamako (announced April 28, 2026) as of May 27, 2026. The March 2026 fuel-corridor truce — under which Mali released 100+ jihadist detainees and JNIM opened fuel supplies to the capital — nominally expires with Eid al-Adha (approximately May 28–June 2, 2026). AP reported on May 27 that Eid livestock prices in Bamako have doubled, with sheep traders stranded in Diema (~345 km west) unable to reach the capital's markets due to ongoing JNIM blockade disruptions. After Eid, JNIM faces no formal truce obligation and retains full structural road-junction control capability to reinstate supply interdiction at will. The US Embassy security alert (issued May 19) remains active through May 31. Three key ongoing fronts: (1) BAMAKO BLOCKADE (Day 29): 3 of 6 supply roads cut (Amnesty International, May 15); WFP suspended ($620M gap, 2M affected); IRC emergency response active; FAO projects 52.8M at acute food insecurity IPC Phase 3+ for June–August lean season — the highest-ever Sahel lean-season projection. Bamako food prices remain +43–65% above pre-siege baselines. Manantali power grid degraded. (2) KIDAL AERIAL CAMPAIGN (ongoing): FAMa/Africa Corps continue striking FLA/JNIM-held Kidal with Su-type fighters and armed drones; no ground-offensive capacity confirmed. FLA holds full city control; Africa Corps operates from Anéfis and Gao. (3) INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY: FIDH/TRIAL International/PALU African Court case (filed April 20) proceeds; Goubré IDP camp massacre (80 killed May 22) and cluster bomb allegations (Tadjmart, May 16–17, RFI-confirmed RBK-500/ShOAB-0.5) sustain IHL documentation pressure. No ceasefire negotiations reported. Al Jazeera (May 26) warned of dangerous regional spillover into coastal states. The post-Eid transition window (May 28–June 5) is assessed as a critical inflection point for the blockade's future course.
